subject: Throughput verification plan for Dedicated reserved pool - acceptance criteria and measurement
messages:
From: Sara Ellis <sara@acmepayments.com>
To: mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acmepayments.com
Date: 2027-06-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated commit — throughput & acceptance questions

Hi Mina,

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement and our infra team need a short, concrete plan we can share with engineering that explains how Redwood will verify the throughput and latency guarantees for the reserved GPU pool under our commit. Specifically we need answers to:

- How you measure tokens/sec and requests/sec (what tooling, synthetic vs captured traces)
- Latency targets (p50/p95/p99) and when they're measured (steady-state vs cold start)
- Warmup/priming requirements (KV cache, prefix caching)
- What constitutes a failed acceptance (sampling window, percent below target)
- A short checklist our SREs can run during onboarding

We've attached a sample production trace from our app (anonymized). Can you respond with a proposed measurement runbook and any minimal changes we should make to the trace?

Thanks,
Sara
Head of Platform Engineering
Acme Payments
From: mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Sara Ellis <sara@acmepayments.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-20T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated commit — throughput & acceptance questions

Sara — great to get the trace, thanks. High level proposal below; we'll follow with a short runbook doc and a one-hour joint test session. Quick answers first, then the proposed measurement steps.

High-level answers:
- Metric definitions: tokens/sec = total server-side decoded tokens / effective measurement window; requests/sec = completed responses / second. We report both at 1m and 5m rolling windows and aggregate percentiles.
- Latency targets: we recommend committing to p95 latency on end-to-end responses (including queueing) and p99 as a soft guardrail. Example ask: p95 <= 350ms, p99 <= 800ms for 4-token median responses (we'll tune based on your trace).
- Warmup: we require a 5–15 minute priming window depending on model KV cache hit-rate; we document warmup steps.
- Failure criteria: a single measurement window (30m) with >10% of samples missing the p95 target triggers an exception and defined remediation.

Proposed measurement runbook (summary):
1) Ingest trace: validate and anonymize (we'll send a sanitized checklist).
2) Map trace to request mix buckets (chat vs short completion vs embeddings).
3) Spike & steady-state phases: run 10m spike (burst at target rps) then 60m steady-state sampling.
4) Warmup: 10m prefix priming run at 25% of target before spike.
5) Instrumentation: we run both service-level timers and agent-level timings (queue, model execution, token emit).
6) Pass/fail: measured p95 for steady-state <= agreed threshold with >=95% of minutes passing.

I'll attach the detailed harness doc and a suggested acceptance script shortly. Karthik — can you confirm whether we should include single-GPU microbench numbers for their target model family (they shared LLM traces but not exact model yet)?

— Mina
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-21T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated commit — throughput & acceptance questions

Looping in some specific measurement guidance. Notes for the runbook: 

- GPU sizing: propose a 4x H100-equivalent pool (N GPUs pinned) as starting point for the commit band they requested. We'll convert to equivalent A100/H100 counts in the doc based on model family.
- Throughput expectation: with our continuous-batching runtime, one H100-equivalent can sustain ~70k tokens/sec for short-chat mixes at 2-token increments (real numbers in attachment microbench). We'll present both tokens/sec and rps curves as a function of batch size.
- Measurement rig: use our harness which can replay captured traces at wall-time fidelity (timestamps preserved). Two parallel methods: 1) replay with preserved inter-arrival times for an apples-to-apples run, and 2) synthetic ramp (controlled rps). Both runs are useful — replay shows realistic behavior; synthetic ramp isolates limits.
- Latency buckets: capture queue_time, model_exec_time, emit_time. Report p50/p90/p95/p99 for each. For acceptance, they want p95 on end-to-end; we should call out p99 and tail behavior as advisory.

I'll add a short table with target numbers per commit band in the doc. Also recommend a small acceptance credit if they fall short on first run (common ask).

— Karthik
Principal Performance Engineer
From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Sara Ellis <sara@acmepayments.com>, mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-23T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated commit — throughput & acceptance questions

Sara — attaching the test harness doc and the suggested acceptance script (also uploaded to Drive). A few practical items from pricing/packaging: 

- Commit bands & discount: we propose two commitment bands for the reserved pool (monthly GPU-hour equivalent): Band A (baseline) and Band B (higher commit). Band A gives a 20% discount on on-demand Dedicated rates, Band B gives 30% and includes a one-time onboarding credit (if initial acceptance run misses targets). The exact discount is negotiable with finance but this is the starting point.
- Acceptance window: one formal acceptance run per onboarding; if we miss, we'll offer a single remediation + re-run within 14 days. If we miss again, a defined credit schedule applies (slides attached).
- Measurement transparency: we will share raw harness logs and minute-level aggregates; your SREs can run the replay in your account if you prefer (we support customer-side runs).

Next steps: schedule the joint run (1 hour) and confirm which model variant they'll use in production (we need to match model config).

Best,
Lauren
Head of Sales Ops, Redwood Inference
From: Sara Ellis <sara@acmepayments.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acmepayments.com, ben@cloudperf.io
Date: 2027-06-25T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated commit — throughput & acceptance questions

Thanks, team — this is helpful and clear. A couple of clarifications before we lock dates: 

1) Can you confirm the pass threshold numerically for Band A? (e.g., steady-state p95 <= 400ms for our trace and >= 95% of minutes within-sla)
2) For the onboarding credit: is that a dollar credit applied to the first billing cycle or a token-hour credit against the commit?
3) We'll bring our SRE and Ben from CloudPerf for the joint run. Can you send the Drive link and the docusign term sheet so procurement can start internal approvals?

If you can reply to these three points today we can aim to run the acceptance on 2027-07-01.

— Sara
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme Payments
